bridal-kanchipuram-saree-trends-2026.title: Bridal Kanchipuram Saree Trends 2026: Pastel Shades, Lightweight Weaves & Minimal Zari
bridal-kanchipuram-saree-trends-2026.alt: Bride in a pastel pink Kanchipuram saree
bridal-kanchipuram-saree-trends-2026.excerpt: Brides are moving beyond classic reds and golds. Here are the Kanchipuram trends shaping weddings this season.

body.p: The Kanchipuram silk saree has been the heart of South Indian weddings for generations. This season, brides are keeping the tradition but making it their own, with softer colours, lighter silks and zari that whispers rather than shouts.

Blush pink, powder blue, mint, lilac and soft peach are everywhere. Pastel Kanchipurams photograph beautifully in daylight ceremonies and pair easily with both gold and diamond jewellery. Many brides choose a pastel body with a contrasting border, such as peach with a deep green, to keep a touch of tradition.
Wedding days are long, and comfort matters. Lighter-weight silks drape gracefully, are easier to move in and still carry the rich sheen Kanchipuram is known for.

list: Ideal for summer and destination weddings
Easier pleating and a softer fall
Comfortable through long rituals and receptions

body.p: Instead of heavy all-over zari, brides are choosing fine zari borders, small buttas and a statement pallu. The result feels modern and refined, and lets the colour and weave speak for themselves.

body.quote: A modern bridal Kanchipuram is less about weight and more about grace.

body.p: Start with your skin tone and the time of your ceremony. Warm pastels like peach and blush suit most skin tones, while cool mint and lavender shine in morning light. Bring your jewellery when you shop, and drape the pallu over your shoulder to see how the colours work together.

manthrakodi-saree-styles-christian-bride.title: Traditional and Modern Manthrakodi Saree Styles for Christian Brides
manthrakodi-saree-styles-christian-bride.excerpt: From classic cream and gold to contemporary pastels, find the Manthrakodi that suits your big day.

body.p: For many Kerala Christian brides, the Manthrakodi is the most meaningful saree they will ever wear. Traditionally gifted by the groom's family and worn for the wedding ceremony, it carries the blessings of both families into the new marriage.

The traditional Manthrakodi is an off-white or cream silk saree with a rich gold zari border, often with touches of red. It is timeless, elegant and perfectly suited to the quiet beauty of a church ceremony.

list: Cream or off-white silk body
Gold zari border, sometimes with red accents
A simple, graceful pallu

body.p: Today's brides are adding their own touch with pastel bodies, silver zari, delicate floral motifs and embroidered blouses. Some choose a lighter Kanchipuram or Banarasi silk for comfort, while keeping the soft palette that defines the Manthrakodi.

body.quote: The Manthrakodi is a gift of love, worn with grace.

body.p: Pair a classic Manthrakodi with pearl or antique gold jewellery and a long veil for a timeless look. For a modern Manthrakodi, a statement blouse with sheer sleeves or embroidered detail adds a contemporary edge.

best-onam-churidar-designs.title: 10 Best Onam Churidar Designs to Shop This Festive Season
best-onam-churidar-designs.excerpt: Kasavu borders, temple motifs and fresh colours: our pick of churidars for Onam celebrations.

body.p: Onam is a time for pookalam, sadhya and celebrations with family and friends. While the kasavu saree is a classic, a churidar is the comfortable, stylish choice for a busy festive day.

list: Classic off-white churidar with a gold kasavu border
Kasavu churidar with a mural-print dupatta
Cream and maroon combination with temple border
Off-white churidar with mango-green accents
Hand-block printed cotton churidar
Kerala mural print kurta with plain bottoms
Pastel churidar with gold zari yoke
Anarkali-style kasavu churidar
Straight-cut churidar with tassel dupatta
Mix-and-match kurta with a contrast kasavu dupatta

body.p: Cotton and cotton-silk blends keep you cool through long celebrations. A straight or A-line kurta is flattering and easy to move in, while an Anarkali adds drama for evening events.

body.quote: Onam style is all about comfort, colour and a touch of gold.

body.p: Complete the look with jhumkas, a few glass bangles and jasmine in your hair. A small gold-toned clutch keeps it festive without being heavy.

traditional-vs-modern-dhavani-designs.title: Traditional vs Modern Dhavani Designs: Which Style Is Right for You?
traditional-vs-modern-dhavani-designs.excerpt: A simple guide to choosing between heritage silk dhavanis and their lighter, modern cousins.

body.p: The dhavani, or half saree, is one of South India's most charming outfits. Made of a long skirt (pavadai), a blouse and a draped dhavani, it is worn for festivals, family functions and important coming-of-age celebrations.
Traditional dhavanis are made in rich silks such as Kanchipuram or Banarasi, with contrasting colours and zari borders. They feel regal and are perfect for weddings, temple visits and ceremonies.

list: Rich silk with zari borders
Bold contrasting colours, such as green with pink or orange with purple
Paired with temple jewellery

body.p: Modern dhavanis use lighter fabrics like organza, georgette and net, with pastel shades, floral prints and embroidered or sequinned blouses. They are easy to wear and ideal for receptions, parties and photo shoots.

body.quote: Traditional or modern, a dhavani always feels like a celebration.

body.p: Choose a traditional silk dhavani for religious ceremonies and family milestones, when heritage matters most. Pick a modern dhavani for evening events or when comfort is a priority. Many families choose one of each, a silk set for the ceremony and a lighter one for the celebration afterwards.

puliyilakkara-set-mundu-onam.title: Why Wearing a Puliyilakkara Set Mundu During Onam Is a Celebration of Kerala Identity
puliyilakkara-set-mundu-onam.alt: Three women in Puliyilakkara set mundu at an Onam celebration
puliyilakkara-set-mundu-onam.excerpt: The story behind the Puliyilakkara border and why it remains at the heart of Onam.

body.p: Few outfits say "Kerala" quite like the set mundu. Simple, elegant and timeless, it is the outfit of choice for Onam, and the Puliyilakkara set mundu holds a special place in that tradition.

body.h: What Is a Puliyilakkara Set Mundu?

body.p: A set mundu is a two-piece garment: the mundu worn as a lower garment and the neriyathu draped over the shoulder. "Puliyilakkara" refers to its distinctive border, a fine pattern inspired by the tamarind leaf, usually woven in a dark contrasting colour against the off-white body.

Handwoven by skilled weavers, the Puliyilakkara border reflects Kerala's deep weaving heritage. Wearing it during Onam is more than a style choice; it is a way of honouring the craft, the community and the spirit of the festival.

body.quote: Every thread of a set mundu carries a story of Kerala.

list: Pair it with a blouse in the border colour, such as green, black or maroon
Add traditional gold jewellery, like a palakka mala or a simple chain
Finish with jasmine in your hair and a small bindi

onam-churidar-designs-college-girls.title: Best Onam Churidar Designs for College Girls and Young Women
onam-churidar-designs-college-girls.alt: Three young women in Onam churidars sitting on steps
onam-churidar-designs-college-girls.excerpt: Easy, comfortable and festive: churidar ideas for campus celebrations and Onam days out.

body.p: Campus Onam celebrations are full of energy: pookalam competitions, games, music and of course group photos. You want to look festive, but you also need to be comfortable all day. A churidar is the perfect answer.

body.h: Easy Styles That Work All Day

list: Short kurta with straight pants for a fresh, modern look
A-line kasavu kurta that is easy to move in
Kurta with a printed mural dupatta for a pop of colour
Co-ord sets in cream and gold for coordinated group photos

body.p: Choose cotton or cotton-blend churidars that you can wear again for other occasions. A plain off-white kurta can be refreshed with a different dupatta each year, giving you a new look without buying a whole new outfit.

body.quote: Festive, comfortable and you: that's the perfect Onam look.

body.p: Oxidised or gold-toned jhumkas, a stack of thin bangles and comfortable sandals are all you need. Keep your bag light so you can enjoy every part of the day.
